sentences.text: The issue involved for adjudication in this appeal is the compensation which can be termed to be just and reasonable that can be awarded to a boy aged about 6 years, who met with a road traffic accident and went into vegetative state due to the injury sustained which position as per the opinion of the doctor who treated him continues through out his life.

The Insurance company is before this court challenging the verdict of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VI at Shivamogga in MVC 1142/2012 dated 31.01.2018, wherein and through which the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.42,79,000/- as compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-VI at Shivamogga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Heard Smt. Geetha Raj, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Kashinath J.D, learned counsel who is representing the claimant.

sentences.text: Making her submission with regard to the merits of the matter, learned counsel for the appellant states that though the fact that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 is not in serious dispute in this appeal and though the liability of the Insurance Company to pay compensation is an admitted fact, yet the amount awarded as compensation by the Tribunal is exorbitant, excessive and beyond permissible limits and therefore the said amount needs considerable reduction.

Learned counsel submits that no evidence is produced by the claimant to show that the NC: 2024:KHC:20732-DB disability is 100% and that there is requirement of incurring medical expenditure in future.
But without considering these aspects, the tribunal awarded an exorbitant sum under all heads and therefore, the amount thus awarded requires to be reduced.

5. Vehemently opposing the submission thus made, learned counsel for the claimant submits that the boy aged about six years, who met with an accident went into unconscious state immediately after the accident and though he was got treated by taking him to different hospitals and though he was kept as inpatient at hospitals on six different occasions, he could not attain normality and the amount of sufferance which the child is bearing cannot be described.
Learned counsel further submits that the child requires an attendant to take care of him for his entire life.

Learned counsel also contends that the child cannot even attend his calls of nature, at least move his leg without the support of any other person, cannot take his bath and cannot attend any other normal activities and NC: 2024:KHC:20732-DB all the activities should be monitored and done by some other person and therefore, for the entire life the boy requires medical attendance as well as an attendant to take care of him and thus, considering all these aspects, the tribunal has awarded a just sum as compensation and therefore the award of the Tribunal needs no interference.
6.

Contradicting the said submission, Smt.Geetha Raj, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal unjustly took the notional income of the boy as Rs.9,000/- applied '18' as multiplier and awarded a sum of Rs.19,44,000/- towards loss of future earnings and the figures applied are therefore
needs to be revisited.
7. Undoubtedly, the Tribunal has taken notional income of Rs.9,000/- per month.
No justification is given by the Tribunal as to how and why it has taken notional income of Rs.9,000/- per month.
However, at the same time, we consider that the Tribunal has not added any amount towards future prospects.

The mandate of law as per the decision of law of the Hon'ble Apex Court in NC:
2024:KHC:20732-DB National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, is that 40% has to be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: 2024:KHC:20732-DB National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, we are of the considered view that the figure arrived at which is awarded as compensation under the head loss of earning capacity i.e., Rs.19,44,000/- needs no interference.

8. Though the learned counsel for the appellant states that the amount awarded as compensation under all other heads is also exorbitant, having regard to the nature of injury sustained, we are unable to differ with the view taken by the Tribunal while awarding compensation.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation under different heads which is detailed as below:

As per the material available on record, the boy aged about six years was admitted at hospital and was given treatment on different occasions totally for 119 days i.e., from 06.08.2011 to 04.09.2011,
03.10.2011 to 10.10.2011, 16.01.2012 to 25.01.2012, 12.04.2015 to 17.04.2015, 26.08.2015 to 31.08.2015 and 07.11.2016 to 12.11.2016.

Coming to the evidence of Cw.1, his evidence is that he is working as Neurosurgeon at Adarsha hospital from August, 2010 and the boy was admitted in their hospital for the first time on 06.08.2011 and he took treatment till 03.09.2011 and at the time of admission, he was identified with head injury and fracture of jaw bone and that he was found in an unconscious state.

The doctor also deposed that CT scan of brain was done, but NC:
2024:KHC:20732-DB no blood clots were found and the fracture to jaw bone must be treated.
However jaw bone plates got infected and thereafter, they were removed.
He also deposed that at the time of discharge the boy was conscious but he was unable to talk.

The doctor stated that he was admitted for the second time and he was compliant of deterioration of neurological status and he was admitted for the third time and when operation was conducted and again he was admitted for the subsequent occasions and treatment was given.
The doctor further deposed that the boy was found with no independent mobility and he had to be carried by an attendant.
He had no capacity to communicate and his condition even after five years of injury did not improve.
The doctor further stated that it is unlikely that he will improve neurological status in future.

The child has no control over his bowel and bladder functions and he requires an attendant to feed and look after his daily The New India vs Master Shobith on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157246164/
4 needs.
He also deposed that the child is in persistent vegetative state.

Stating that in a similarly placed situation, the Hon'ble Apex Court has granted a sum of Rupees Fifty lakhs as compensation, the learned counsel for the claimant produced decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case between Master Ayush vs. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 375.

entities.text: Master Ayush vs. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 375
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Hon'ble Apex Court dealt with a situation where a boy aged about five years met with a road traffic accident and was found to be a known case of Traumatic Paraplegia.
In the said case, when the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.18,24,000/- as compensation, the High Court reduced the same to Rs.13,46,805/-.

In the appeal, the Hon'ble Apex Court considering the state of the injured child,
awarded a sum of Rs.49,93,000/- as compensation.
11. Admittedly, the loss which includes mental and physical cannot be assessed in terms of money.
Here is a case where a boy aged about six years lost his entire future due to the injury sustained and he became - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:20732-DB dependent on others.
We cannot expect the parents to take care of the child, as no one can presume that the parents will live till the life time of the child.

Also in the light of the incapacity and incapability of the child to perform his own functions, one cannot expect that he on attaining the age of majority would be in a position to marry and lead marital life.
The Doctor i.e., Cw.1 has clearly stated that claimant is in persistent vegetative state.
Therefore, we are of the considered view that the amount awarded as compensation by the Tribunal can neither be termed to be exorbitant nor excessive.
Therefore, the ultimate conclusion of this Court is that in this appeal lacks merits and hence to be dismissed so far as award of the compensation is concerned.

12. However, taking into consideration the submission made by Smt.Geetha Raj with regard to award of interest at the rate of 7% per annum, this court is of the view that the same is required to be reduced to 6% per annum.

Resultantly, the following:
- 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC:20732-DB  ORDER  (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
